requiredFindings.title: Bound emitted candidate bodies by the retained envelope schema

location.section: item 14a sourceBodies and complete/group-bound rows; item 11; E3-T9

requiredFindings.problem: The table is not complete against CandidateProducerResultV1: sourceBodies is capped at 100,000 rows, but no proposed bound limits the union of body ids in emitted groups to that size. The listed per-group and per-universe group limits permit a complete result whose required sourceBodies array is schema-invalid. Dropping source-body rows would violate group custody; emitting an empty complete result would conceal work; treating normal capacity exhaustion as backend-fault would use the wrong route.

evidence.note: The declared clone bounds are 4,096 members per group and 1,000,000 groups per universe; no emitted-body union bound is listed.
One sourceBodies row is required for every distinct id in an emitted group. Parsed paths and groups within the stated bounds yield complete, null/null.
groupDigests permits 1,000,000 entries, while sourceBodies permits only 100,000 entries. The executed carrier is explicitly this exact retained schema.
Each CloneCandidateGroupV2 may contain 4,096 unique members.
Retained group members need matching sourceBodies and snapshot/source-census custody; adapter maps cannot supply missing rows.

25 disjoint groups of 4,096 members produce 102,400 distinct emitted ids. Every group fits and 25 is below the group-count limit, but the required sourceBodies array exceeds 100,000. This is cardinality arithmetic, not an executed parser fixture.
E3-T9 covers parse bounds and group size/count, but no envelope body-union exhaustion.

requiredFindings.fix: Add the retained carrier's 100,000-source-body limit to the candidate bounds and case table. Derive the union of ids of the groups actually retained. If the next whole group would exceed it, withhold that group under a deterministic declared order, emit a partial/budget-exhausted/null result (subject to the existing higher-priority deficiency selection), and keep one custody row per retained id. Do not cut a connected component or omit its custody rows. Alternatively change the envelope limit only through an explicit execution-input successor with its own review. Add E3-T9 boundary controls for 100,000 and 100,001 distinct emitted ids across individually valid groups, checked by the existing execution-input owner.

requiredFindings.title: Include normalization records in the closed member traversal

location.section: item 4 closed tree and manifest/definition shapes; item 5 A3/A6; item 14

requiredFindings.problem: The new closed-tree rule requires every tree member to be named by the bundle manifest or a grammar definition, but the required IE normalization specification map and its level specifications are named by neither record shape. The bundle normalizer points to a different fixed file. A truthful closure carrying the required normalization records is therefore refused as unlisted; omitting them violates item 4 and the identity owner. Listing them as upstream build sources or third-party notices would misstate their role.

evidence.note: The closure must contain the fixed normalization specification-map and its level files. The code/data definition shapes have no normalization-map/level member field, and every member must be named by manifest or definition.
The manifest's normalizer specificationPath is fixed by A3 to opensip-interface/grammar/normalizer.v1.json. A6 accepts only members named by that manifest or a grammar definition.
The level specifications are expressly required in this same closure at IE's fixed specification-map path.

For syntax-only bodies the grammar closure owns opensip-interface/normalization/specification-map.v1.json and the level digests it maps. The SyntaxGrammarBundle normalizer digest retains a different native-admission meaning; it does not select a level specification.
The machine-readable normalizationSpecificationLaw requires the fixed map and referenced specification digests in the owning tree.

The required path is opensip-interface/normalization/specification-map.v1.json, while the only manifest normalizer path is opensip-interface/grammar/normalizer.v1.json. No normalization-map or level-file member list appears in the declared manifest/code-definition shapes.

requiredFindings.fix: Define the closed traversal to include the IE normalization map and its referenced level records, with exact path/digest/retained-byte joins. Either add an explicit manifest member description for the map/levels, or admit the fixed IE map as an additional declared root and allow exactly its validated level-digest references to resolve to tree members. Keep the native normalizer specification separate and reject genuinely unrelated members. Update item 4, A3/A6, SYN-NS and the closure controls together. Add a positive complete closure containing the mandatory map/levels, plus negatives for a missing map, a missing/mismatched level member and an unrelated extra file. Keep both T-wasm and T-native subject to the same retention law.

requiredFindings.title: Remove the false NativeCause mirror targets in startup reasons
requiredFindings.problem: SYN-1(f) calls provider-startup.schemas.v1.json:83 and :610 NativeCause copies and directs the cause addition there. Those locations belong to the TypeScript post-Analyze Unavailable.reason vocabulary, not NativeCause. The startup schema defines no copy of the 14-member NativeCause enum; its Coverage entries reference the native owner. Treating these six-member reason lists as mirrors would widen a negotiated TS2 terminal vocabulary and misroute a syntax parse failure as provider unavailability, beyond the intended cause extension.

evidence.note: SYN-1(f) explicitly targets NativeCause copies at provider-startup.schemas.v1.json:83 and :610.
E2s includes startup-v1 among schema sources to which SYN-1/SYN-1F are applied.
The first location is x-opensip-startup-law.postAnalyzeReasons.typescript-semantic. The terminal Coverage entries carry provider-unavailable for an Unavailable terminal.
The second location is TypeScriptUnavailableV2.properties.reason.enum. Its Coverage array references the owner CoverageResultV3 by urn; it does not redefine NativeCause.
NativeCause is a separate 14-member typed cause enum beside DeficiencyV2.

No exact NativeCause copy exists in startup. Its two targeted six-member lists equal each other, but four of those reason strings are not NativeCause members. Sharing capability-missing and node-modules-outside-read-set does not make the vocabularies mirrors.

requiredFindings.fix: Correct SYN-1(f) to follow actual NativeCause definitions/references, and remove the instruction to append source-parse-error to the post-Analyze Unavailable reason lists. Keep the foundation five-copy mirror list and the native owner enum/allowed-causes update; regenerate referenced carriers through the normal closed generation lane. Adjust E2s's startup source scope accordingly. If a startup-reason change is separately intended, name and justify that protocol successor and its mappings rather than treating it as enum synchronization. Require a selector-level mirror check and a control showing that source-parse-error is accepted as a lawful input-closure-incomplete Coverage/candidate cause while the Unavailable.reason vocabulary stays its existing closed set.
